senses.en: showing kindness or forgiveness to someone one could punish
giving relief from suffering

ex.en: The king was merciful and spared the prisoners' lives.
ex.zh: 國王很仁慈，饒了囚犯們的性命。

senses.en: showing no mercy; cruel

ex.en: The desert sun was merciless, and we ran out of water by noon.
ex.zh: 沙漠的太陽毫不留情，我們中午前就把水喝光了。

senses.en: attractive in a cheap or showy way but having no real value

ex.en: Critics dismissed the film as meretricious entertainment with no real ideas.
ex.zh: 評論家認為這部電影只是華而不實、沒有真正思想的娛樂。

parts.m: prostitute 妓女（拉丁文 meretrix，mer 賺取）

root.note: 像妓女般靠外表招攬 → 俗豔、華而不實

senses.en: to hold someone's attention completely; to fascinate
(dated) to hypnotize

ex.en: The dancer's graceful movements seemed to mesmerize the audience.
ex.zh: 舞者優雅的動作似乎讓觀眾看得入迷。

parts.m: Franz Mesmer 梅斯梅爾（18 世紀催眠術始祖）

root.note: 用梅斯梅爾的催眠術 → 迷住

senses.en: plural of monsieur; used as a formal title for two or more men (abbreviated Messrs.)
senses.zh: 先生們（monsieur 的複數；縮寫 Messrs.）

ex.en: The letter was addressed to messieurs Dupont and Martin.
ex.zh: 這封信是寫給杜邦先生和馬丁先生的。

root.note: 我的大人們 → 先生們

mn: 法文唸 [meˋsjø]，英文縮寫 Messrs. 則唸 [ˋmɛsɚz]。

senses.en: a hard, shiny substance such as iron, gold, or copper

ex.en: Copper is a metal that conducts electricity very well.
ex.zh: 銅是一種導電性極佳的金屬。

mn: metal（金屬）和 mettle（勇氣）同音，原本是同一個字。

senses.en: the science of metals and how to extract and use them

ex.en: Advances in metallurgy allowed engineers to build lighter airplanes.
ex.zh: 冶金學的進步讓工程師能造出更輕的飛機。

root.note: 處理金屬的工作 → 冶金

senses.en: a complete change of form, as from caterpillar to butterfly
a complete change in character or appearance

ex.en: The old warehouse underwent a metamorphosis into a modern art center.
ex.zh: 那座老倉庫徹底蛻變成一座現代藝術中心。

root.note: 形狀的改變 → 變態；蛻變

senses.en: a figure of speech that describes something by calling it something else
a thing that symbolizes something else

ex.en: "Time is money" is a common metaphor in English.
ex.zh: 「時間就是金錢」是英文裡常見的隱喻。

root.note: 把意義轉移到別的事物上 → 隱喻

mn: simile（明喻）用 like/as；metaphor（暗喻）直接說 A 是 B。

senses.en: relating to metaphysics; concerned with abstract ideas about reality
beyond the physical world; supernatural

ex.en: The class debated metaphysical questions about whether time really exists.
ex.zh: 班上辯論了時間是否真實存在這類形而上的問題。

root.note: 超越自然的 → 形而上的

senses.en: a person who studies metaphysics

ex.en: The metaphysician argued that the mind cannot be reduced to the brain.
ex.zh: 那位形而上學家主張心靈無法化約為大腦。

root.note: 研究超越自然之事的人

senses.en: the branch of philosophy that studies the nature of reality and existence

ex.en: Aristotle's metaphysics explores what it means for something to exist.
ex.zh: 亞里斯多德的形而上學探討事物存在的意義。

root.note: 原指亞里斯多德排在《物理學》之後的著作 → 形而上學

senses.en: to hand out punishment or justice (usually mete out)
senses.zh: 給予（懲罰）；分配（常用 mete out）

ex.en: The court will mete out a harsh sentence to repeat offenders.
ex.zh: 法院將對累犯處以重刑。

root.note: 量好分配出去 → 給予（懲罰）

senses.en: the passing of the soul into another body after death; reincarnation

ex.en: Pythagoras believed in metempsychosis and refused to eat meat.
ex.zh: 畢達哥拉斯相信靈魂轉世，所以拒絕吃肉。

root.note: 靈魂換到（另一個身體）裡 → 轉世

senses.en: a figure of speech in which something is called by the name of something closely related to it

ex.en: Using "the White House" to mean the president is an example of metonymy.
ex.zh: 用「白宮」來指美國總統就是轉喻的一個例子。

root.note: 換一個名字來稱呼 → 轉喻

senses.en: relating to the system of measurement based on meters and kilograms
a standard of measurement used to judge performance

ex.en: Most countries use the metric system for weights and distances.
ex.zh: 大多數國家的重量和距離都使用公制。

senses.en: a device that marks time with a regular tick for musicians

ex.en: The piano teacher set the metronome to a slow beat.
ex.zh: 鋼琴老師把節拍器調到慢速。

root.note: 規律地測量（拍子）→ 節拍器

senses.en: a very large and important city

ex.en: Tokyo is a bustling metropolis of more than thirteen million people.
ex.zh: 東京是一座人口超過一千三百萬的繁華大都市。

root.note: 母城 → 首要的大城市

senses.en: relating to a large city and its surrounding area

ex.en: The Taipei metropolitan area has an excellent subway system.
ex.zh: 台北都會區有非常好的捷運系統。

senses.en: courage and strength of character in difficult situations

ex.en: The difficult final match tested the young player's mettle.
ex.zh: 艱難的決賽考驗了這名年輕球員的勇氣。

mn: 原是 metal 的另一種拼法：像金屬一樣硬的性格 → 勇氣。片語 test one's mettle。

senses.en: full of spirit and courage

ex.en: The mettlesome horse refused to stand still at the starting gate.
ex.zh: 那匹精力旺盛的馬在起跑閘門前不肯站定。

senses.en: a small place or situation that has the typical features of something much larger

ex.en: The classroom was a microcosm of society as a whole.
ex.zh: 這間教室就是整個社會的縮影。

senses.en: an instrument for measuring very small distances or thicknesses
[ˋmaɪkroˏmitɚ] one millionth of a meter; a micron

ex.en: The engineer used a micrometer to check the thickness of the wire.
ex.zh: 工程師用測微計檢查電線的粗細。

root.note: 測量微小東西的工具；百萬分之一公尺

senses.en: a device that changes sound into electrical signals so it can be recorded or amplified

ex.en: Please speak into the microphone so everyone can hear you.
ex.zh: 請對著麥克風說話，讓每個人都聽得到。

root.note: 讓微小的聲音放大的裝置

senses.en: an instrument used to see very small objects

ex.en: We looked at onion cells under the microscope in biology class.
ex.zh: 我們在生物課上用顯微鏡觀察洋蔥細胞。

mn: under the microscope 也可比喻「受到仔細檢視」。

senses.en: so small that it can only be seen with a microscope
senses.zh: 極小的；顯微鏡才看得到的

senses.en: extremely detailed

ex.en: Microscopic organisms live in every drop of pond water.
ex.zh: 每一滴池塘水中都有微生物。

root.note: 要用顯微鏡看的 → 極小的

senses.en: the use of microscopes to study small objects

ex.en: Electron microscopy revealed the structure of the virus.
ex.zh: 電子顯微鏡技術揭示了病毒的結構。

senses.en: the middle of summer, around the summer solstice in late June

ex.en: Swedes celebrate midsummer by dancing around a flower-covered pole.
ex.zh: 瑞典人在仲夏節時繞著綴滿花朵的柱子跳舞慶祝。

senses.en: a person trained to help women during childbirth

ex.en: The midwife stayed with the mother through the long night of labor.
ex.zh: 助產士整夜陪著分娩中的母親。

root.note: 陪著產婦的婦人 → 助產士

senses.en: a person's look or manner, showing their mood or character

ex.en: The old judge had a serious mien that made lawyers nervous.
ex.zh: 老法官神情嚴肅，讓律師們都很緊張。

senses.en: a person who moves from one place to another, especially to find work
moving regularly from place to place

ex.en: Each migrant worker sends part of his wages home to his family.
ex.zh: 每位移工都會把部分薪水寄回家給家人。

senses.en: (of animals) to move from one region to another with the seasons
(of people) to move to another place to live or work

ex.en: Many birds migrate south to escape the cold winter.
ex.zh: 許多鳥類往南遷徙以躲避寒冷的冬天。

senses.en: moving from one place to another with the seasons

ex.en: The wetland is an important stop for migratory birds.
ex.zh: 這片濕地是候鳥重要的中途站。

senses.en: the number of miles traveled or a vehicle can travel per gallon of fuel
(informal) benefit or advantage gained from something

ex.en: This used car has very low mileage for its age.
ex.zh: 以車齡來說，這輛二手車的里程數很低。

senses.en: aggressively active in support of a cause
a person who uses aggressive or violent methods for a cause

ex.en: A militant group claimed responsibility for the attack.
ex.zh: 一個武裝組織宣稱對這起攻擊事件負責。

root.note: 像士兵一樣戰鬥的 → 激進的

senses.en: the belief that a country should have strong armed forces and use them aggressively

ex.en: The rise of militarism in the 1930s led to war in Asia.
ex.zh: 1930 年代軍國主義的興起導致了亞洲的戰爭。

senses.en: (of a fact or circumstance) to have a strong effect in preventing something (usually militate against)
senses.zh: （事實、情況）阻礙；產生不利影響（常用 militate against）

ex.en: His lack of experience may militate against his chances of promotion.
ex.zh: 他經驗不足可能不利於他的升遷機會。

root.note: 像士兵一樣作戰 → 起作用（常指不利）

mn: 別和 mitigate（減輕）搞混：militate against 是「對……不利」。

senses.en: a military force of ordinary citizens rather than professional soldiers

ex.en: The town formed a militia to defend itself against raiders.
ex.zh: 小鎮組織了民兵以抵禦掠奪者。

root.note: 一群（平民）士兵 → 民兵

senses.en: the galaxy containing our solar system, seen as a band of light across the night sky

ex.en: Far from city lights, we could clearly see the Milky Way.
ex.zh: 遠離城市燈光，我們能清楚看見銀河。

mn: 希臘神話說是女神赫拉的乳汁灑在天上形成的，所以叫「牛奶路」。

senses.en: a cereal plant with very small seeds, grown for food

ex.en: The indigenous village holds a festival to celebrate the millet harvest.
ex.zh: 這個原住民部落舉辦祭典慶祝小米豐收。

senses.en: to copy someone's voice, movements, or behavior, often to amuse
a person or animal that copies others

ex.en: Parrots can mimic human speech surprisingly well.
ex.zh: 鸚鵡模仿人類說話的能力好得驚人。

parts.m: imitate 模仿（希臘文 mimos 演員）

senses.en: very small; a small-scale version of something
a very small, detailed painting or model

ex.en: The museum displays a miniature model of the ancient city.
ex.zh: 博物館展示了那座古城的微縮模型。

senses.en: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount
to make something seem less important than it is

ex.en: Wear a seat belt to minimize the risk of serious injury.
ex.zh: 繫上安全帶，把重傷的風險降到最低。

senses.en: an unimportant follower who obeys a powerful person

ex.en: The villain sent a minion to steal the plans.
ex.zh: 反派派一個手下去偷計畫書。

senses.en: (usually plural) the giving of help or care

ex.en: Thanks to the nurse's gentle ministration, the patient soon recovered.
ex.zh: 多虧護理師的細心照料，病人很快就康復了。

senses.en: a government department led by a minister
the work or office of a religious minister

ex.en: The Ministry of Education announced changes to the college entrance exam.
ex.zh: 教育部宣布了大學入學考試的改革。

root.note: 服務（國家、上帝）的機構或職務

senses.en: the smaller part of a group, less than half
a group differing in race, religion, or culture from the larger population

ex.en: Only a minority of students voted against the new dress code.
ex.zh: 只有少數學生投票反對新的服裝規定。

senses.en: a period of sixty seconds
(plural) the official written record of a meeting
[maɪˋnjut] extremely small; very detailed

ex.en: The scientist noticed a minute difference between the two samples.
ex.zh: 科學家注意到兩個樣本之間有極細微的差異。

root.note: 被分得很小的 → 微小的；小時再細分 → 分鐘

senses.en: a small or trivial detail (usually plural minutiae)
senses.zh: 細節；瑣事（常用複數 minutiae）

ex.en: The manager gets lost in every minutia and ignores the big picture.
ex.zh: 那位經理總是迷失在每個細枝末節中，忽略了大局。

senses.en: an optical illusion, such as seeing water in a desert, caused by hot air
a hope or wish that cannot come true

ex.en: The lake in the distance turned out to be a mirage.
ex.zh: 遠處的湖泊結果只是海市蜃樓。

root.note: 看到令人驚奇的景象 → 幻影

senses.en: an unfortunate incident or accident

ex.en: The novel follows the comic misadventure of two tourists lost in Paris.
ex.zh: 這部小說描寫兩個觀光客在巴黎迷路的爆笑倒楣遭遇。

mn: 法律用語 death by misadventure：意外死亡。

senses.en: disliking and distrusting other people
senses.zh: 厭惡人類的；憤世嫉俗的

ex.en: The misanthropic old man refused to speak to his neighbors.
ex.zh: 那個憤世嫉俗的老人拒絕和鄰居說話。

senses.en: a general dislike and distrust of people

ex.en: Years of betrayal had turned his disappointment into misanthropy.
ex.zh: 多年被背叛的經歷，讓他的失望變成了對人性的厭惡。

mn: 這裡的 mis 是希臘文「恨」，不是英文字首 mis-（錯）。

senses.en: to misunderstand words or actions

ex.en: Readers often misapprehend the author's irony as sincerity.
ex.zh: 讀者常把作者的反諷誤解成真心話。

senses.en: to behave badly

ex.en: Children often misbehave when they are tired or hungry.
ex.zh: 孩子累了或餓了時常常會不乖。

senses.en: bad or unacceptable behavior

ex.en: The teacher would not tolerate any misbehavior during the field trip.
ex.zh: 老師在校外教學期間不容許任何不當行為。

senses.en: playfully causing trouble
intended to cause harm or trouble

ex.en: The mischievous puppy chewed up my new shoes.
ex.zh: 那隻頑皮的小狗把我的新鞋咬爛了。

parts.m: come to an end, head 結果（古法文 chever）

root.note: 帶來壞結果 → 惹麻煩的；淘氣的

mn: 常被誤唸成 mis-CHEE-vee-ous；正確是三個音節 [ˋmɪstʃɪvəs]。

senses.en: to count wrongly
a wrong count

ex.en: Be careful not to miscount the votes this time.
ex.zh: 這次小心別把票數算錯了。

senses.en: a person who behaves badly or breaks the law

ex.en: Police are searching for the miscreant who spray-painted the school walls.
ex.zh: 警方正在搜尋在學校牆上噴漆的那名歹徒。

root.note: 原指信錯宗教的人 → 惡棍

senses.en: a wicked or illegal act

ex.en: He spent years trying to make up for a single misdeed in his youth.
ex.zh: 他花了好多年來彌補年輕時犯下的一件錯事。

senses.en: a minor crime, less serious than a felony
a wrong or improper act

ex.en: Shoplifting a candy bar is usually treated as a misdemeanor.
ex.zh: 偷一條巧克力棒通常被視為輕罪。

senses.en: a person who hoards money and hates spending it

ex.en: The old miser lived in poverty despite his huge fortune.
ex.zh: 那個老守財奴雖然家財萬貫，卻過得很窮困。

root.note: 可憐的人 → 捨不得花錢的人

mn: 和 misery（悲慘）同源：守財奴過得很悲慘。

senses.en: a small accident or piece of bad luck

ex.en: Apart from one minor mishap, the trip went smoothly.
ex.zh: 除了一個小意外之外，這趟旅行很順利。

senses.en: to understand or explain something wrongly

ex.en: It is easy to misinterpret a short text message.
ex.zh: 簡短的文字訊息很容易被誤解。

senses.en: to put something somewhere and then forget where it is
senses.zh: 把……放錯地方；一時找不到

ex.en: I always mislay my keys when I'm in a hurry.
ex.zh: 我一匆忙就會忘記把鑰匙放在哪裡。

senses.en: to manage badly or wrongly

ex.en: If you mismanage the budget, the project will run out of money.
ex.zh: 如果預算管理不當，這個計畫就會把錢用光。

senses.en: a wrong or inaccurate name or term

ex.en: "Koala bear" is a misnomer, because the koala is not a bear.
ex.zh: 「無尾熊」叫 koala bear 是誤稱，因為無尾熊並不是熊。

senses.en: hatred of marriage

ex.en: The bachelor's misogamy was well known among his friends.
ex.zh: 這位單身漢厭惡婚姻是朋友們都知道的事。

senses.en: dislike of, contempt for, or prejudice against women

ex.en: The article criticized the misogyny in some online communities.
ex.zh: 這篇文章批評了一些網路社群中的厭女現象。

senses.en: to put something in the wrong place and lose it temporarily
to give trust or affection to the wrong person

ex.en: Try not to misplace your passport while traveling.
ex.zh: 旅行時盡量別把護照弄丟了。

senses.en: to give a false or misleading account of something

ex.en: The ad seems to misrepresent how long the battery actually lasts.
ex.zh: 這則廣告似乎誇大了電池實際的續航時間。

senses.en: bad or unfair government; disorder
to govern badly

ex.en: Years of misrule left the country poor and divided.
ex.zh: 多年的惡政讓這個國家貧窮又分裂。

senses.en: a book containing the prayers and texts for Catholic Mass

ex.en: The priest opened the missal and began to read the prayers.
ex.zh: 神父打開彌撒書，開始誦讀禱文。

senses.en: a weapon that is self-propelled or guided and carries explosives
an object thrown or shot at a target

ex.en: The navy tested a new missile over the ocean.
ex.zh: 海軍在海上試射了一枚新型飛彈。

root.note: 可以投擲出去的東西 → 飛彈

senses.en: a letter or written message, especially a long or official one

ex.en: She received a long missive from her aunt full of family news.
ex.zh: 她收到阿姨寄來的一封長信，寫滿了家裡的消息。

senses.en: lack of trust; suspicion
to be suspicious of

ex.en: There is deep mistrust between the two neighboring countries.
ex.zh: 這兩個鄰國之間存在很深的不信任。

senses.en: full of or covered with mist
(of eyes) filled with tears; (of memories) vague

ex.en: We hiked up the misty mountain early in the morning.
ex.zh: 我們一大早爬上霧氣繚繞的山。

senses.en: to fail to understand correctly

ex.en: Please don't misunderstand me; I really like your idea.
ex.zh: 請別誤會，我真的很喜歡你的點子。

senses.en: to use something wrongly or for a bad purpose
[mɪsˋjus] the wrong or improper use of something

ex.en: Officials must not misuse public money for personal travel.
ex.zh: 官員不得濫用公款從事私人旅遊。

senses.en: a tiny creature related to spiders, often living on plants or animals
a very small amount; a small child

ex.en: A single dust mite is too small to see without a microscope.
ex.zh: 一隻塵蟎小到沒有顯微鏡就看不見。

mn: a mite + 形容詞（口語）表示「有點」，例如 a mite tired。

senses.en: a tall pointed hat worn by bishops
a joint made by cutting two pieces at an angle so they fit together

ex.en: The bishop wore a white miter embroidered with gold.
ex.zh: 主教戴著一頂繡金的白色法冠。

senses.en: to make something less severe, serious, or painful

ex.en: Planting trees can help mitigate the effects of urban heat.
ex.zh: 種樹有助於減緩都市熱島效應。

parts.m: soft, mild 柔和（拉丁文 mitis）

mn: mitigating circumstances：可減輕罪責的情節。

senses.en: techniques or systems for improving memory

ex.en: Mnemonics can make memorizing vocabulary much easier.
ex.zh: 記憶術能讓背單字容易許多。

mn: 開頭的 m 不發音；這本 App 裡的 mn 欄位就是 mnemonic 的縮寫。

senses.en: a deep, wide ditch filled with water around a castle
a lasting advantage that protects a business from competitors

ex.en: A drawbridge crossed the moat to the castle gate.
ex.zh: 一座吊橋跨越護城河通往城堡大門。

senses.en: rule or domination by the masses or a mob

ex.en: Critics warned that the angry protests could turn into mobocracy.
ex.zh: 批評者警告，憤怒的抗議可能演變成暴民政治。

senses.en: a soft leather shoe without a heel, originally worn by Native Americans
senses.zh: （北美原住民的）鹿皮軟鞋；莫卡辛鞋

ex.en: Each moccasin was decorated with colorful beads.
ex.zh: 每隻鹿皮軟鞋上都綴著彩色串珠。

senses.en: teasing or making fun of someone
an absurd or worthless imitation of something

ex.en: The unfair trial was a mockery of justice.
ex.zh: 這場不公正的審判是對正義的嘲弄。

mn: make a mockery of：使……成為笑柄。

senses.en: the avoidance of excess or extremes

ex.en: Chocolate is fine if you eat it in moderation.
ex.zh: 巧克力只要適量吃就沒問題。

senses.en: a person who leads a discussion or debate
a person who monitors an online forum

ex.en: The moderator asked each candidate the same three questions.
ex.zh: 主持人向每位候選人提出相同的三個問題。

root.note: 維持分寸的人 → 主持人

senses.en: the quality or condition of being modern

ex.en: The city blends ancient tradition with striking modernity.
ex.zh: 這座城市融合了古老傳統與鮮明的現代感。

parts.m: just now 剛才（拉丁文 modo）

root.note: 屬於現在的性質 → 現代性

senses.en: to adapt something to modern needs or habits; to update

ex.en: The government plans to modernize the old railway system.
ex.zh: 政府計劃將老舊的鐵路系統現代化。

senses.en: a small change made to improve something

ex.en: With one small modification, the recipe becomes vegan.
ex.zh: 只要稍作修改，這道食譜就能變成全素料理。

senses.en: to make partial changes to something
(grammar) to describe or limit the meaning of a word

ex.en: We had to modify our plans because of the typhoon.
ex.zh: 因為颱風，我們不得不修改計畫。

senses.en: fashionable; stylish

ex.en: The café is full of modish young people taking photos of their drinks.
ex.zh: 咖啡廳裡滿是替飲料拍照的時髦年輕人。

senses.en: to adjust or regulate the level or tone of something
(music) to change from one key to another

ex.en: A good speaker learns to modulate her voice to keep listeners interested.
ex.zh: 好的演說者會學習調整聲音，讓聽眾保持興趣。

root.note: 做小幅度的尺度調整 → 調節

senses.en: to calm someone's anger or anxiety

ex.en: The airline offered free meals to mollify the angry passengers.
ex.zh: 航空公司提供免費餐點來安撫憤怒的乘客。

senses.en: (of an animal) to shed old feathers, hair, or skin
the process of molting

ex.en: Snakes molt several times a year as they grow.
ex.zh: 蛇在成長過程中一年會脫好幾次皮。

root.note: 改變（外皮）→ 換毛；蛻皮

senses.en: lasting for a very short time

ex.en: There was a momentary silence before the audience burst into applause.
ex.zh: 觀眾爆出掌聲之前，現場安靜了片刻。

mn: momentary（短暫的）vs. momentous（重大的）：多了 ous 就變重要了。

senses.en: very important because of its effect on the future

ex.en: Choosing a college is a momentous decision.
ex.zh: 選擇大學是一個重大的決定。

parts.m: importance, movement 重要性（拉丁文 momentum）

senses.en: the force that keeps a moving object moving
the strength or speed gained by a developing process

ex.en: The campaign gained momentum after the popular singer joined it.
ex.zh: 那位人氣歌手加入後，這項運動的聲勢越來越大。

root.note: 移動的力量 → 動量；氣勢
